experiment_ids: All 80 stable-family experiments in run_outputs.json: 20 datasets crossed with S_balanced, S_alpha_slow, S_eta_slow, and S_near_boundary
limitations_and_unperformed_work: No general convergence theorem is claimed.
No population-consistency, universal causal-identification, or Transformer claim was tested.
The target was sample 2SLS; truth errors were descriptive only and were not used for fitting or initialization.
After two recorded 120-second timeouts, the final design used 20 datasets and a 10,000-iteration stable horizon; the deviation is recorded in experiment_configs.json.
No higher-precision or longer follow-up was run for the two slow finite-horizon cases.
hypothesis_evidence_map.short_conclusion: Supported for the tested identified Gaussian samples, subject to finite-horizon and numerical-precision qualifications. All 80 within-region runs completed 10,000 iterations, and 78/80 ended with relative beta error below 1e-8 against sample 2SLS. Median final beta errors were 1.75e-15 (balanced), 8.78e-15 (alpha-slow), 3.38e-15 (eta-slow), and 2.89e-15 (near-boundary). The two slower cases were consistent with severe conditioning and Lambda close to one: default seed 6 under alpha-slow ended at 1.43e-5 with Lambda=0.998913 and cond(A)=91.98; near-square seed 102 under eta-slow ended at beta error 1.39e-8 and theta error 1.10e-6 with Lambda=0.998861 and cond(B)=87.79. Twelve usable alpha-slow late-window fits had median fitted factor 0.994558, close to median Lambda 0.993716. Most faster traces reached the floating-point floor before the fitting window, so their rate fits were marked unsupported rather than forced.
hypothesis_evidence_map.uncertainty: Finite-sample evidence covers 20 generated datasets across five regimes. Only 17/80 predeclared late-window fits were supported because most errors reached approximately 1e-15 before the fit window; isolated fits at that floor are not interpreted as rate evidence. Observed condition numbers ranged from 5.23 to 91.98 for A and 1.87 to 87.79 for B.

experiment_ids: All 80 stable-family and 60 outside-family experiments in run_outputs.json
limitations_and_unperformed_work: No claim is made that every setting outside the candidate region diverges.
No dense boundary sweep was performed, so no sharp empirical stability frontier was estimated.
The 1e100 cutoff is an operational safeguard, not a mathematical definition of divergence.
The 95%-of-boundary setting was often fast because its extreme-eigenvalue factors were near 0.9; its label denotes proximity of the step size to the bound, not necessarily slow convergence.
hypothesis_evidence_map.short_conclusion: Supported for the tested step-size contrasts. Setting alpha to 5% of its upper bound made gamma the Lambda bottleneck in 18/20 datasets; setting eta to 5% made kappa the bottleneck in 18/20. Paired iteration-200 errors showed the deliberately slowed block generally lagging balanced and 95%-of-boundary settings, with particularly slow theta behavior in ill-conditioned near-square samples, although coupled transients prevented a universal ordering. Outside the candidate region, alpha at 101% completed 2,000 iterations in all 20 datasets but produced enormous beta errors (median 2.00e15; range 2.43e13 to 3.28e16). Eta at 101% and both steps at 125% crossed the operational 1e100 divergence threshold in all 20 datasets. Thus completion alone did not indicate convergence, and Lambda identified the unstable or limiting block in these tested settings.
hypothesis_evidence_map.uncertainty: Comparisons were paired within each dataset, but covered only four within-region and three outside-region step choices. Lambda is an asymptotic block diagnostic and does not describe every nonlinear coupled transient. Outside-region evidence covers 20 datasets and at most 2,000 iterations.

method_fidelity.statement: The fixed iteration uses zero initialization, positive constant step sizes, unnormalized gradient sums, and simultaneous updates from old theta and old beta. Cached products B=Z.T@Z, C=Z.T@X, and d=Z.T@Y are algebraically equivalent to the specified updates. Exact least-squares solutions are used only as comparators and diagnostics.

omissions: No formal theorem or universal stability claim.
No higher-precision or extended-horizon follow-up for the two slow stable cases.
Formal isolation was not independently verified; the successful execution record reports CPU-only execution with exit code 0.
